seo.title: LTX 2.5 Pro AI Video Generator for Production Work
seo.description: Choose LTX 2.5 Pro for current production-focused text, image and source-audio video, with exact workflow limits, prompt guidance and canonical pricing.

overview: LTX 2.5 Pro is the current default production route for the LTX family. It supports text-to-video, image-to-video and a separate source-audio-driven workflow at 720p or 1080p. Lightricks owns LTX, while MaxVideoAI distributes these endpoints through Fal for the launch.

hero.title: LTX 2.5 Pro
hero.subtitle: Move a locked brief into production-focused text, image or source-audio video at 720p or 1080p with native generated sound on creation modes.
hero.paragraph: Choose Pro when the concept and continuity anchors are already defined and the team needs the current LTX production route. Text and image modes render from six to ten seconds, while audio-to-video follows the validated source-audio duration. Lightricks owns the model; Fal distributes MaxVideoAI execution for this release.

features.title: Current LTX production position
features.body: Pro is the family default for approved production briefs, while Fast remains the sibling for exploratory loops. This is a workflow distinction, not an unsupported claim that one variant wins every visual category.

features.title: Short controlled generation
features.body: Text and image modes support six, eight or ten-second outputs at 720p or 1080p. Use that bounded window for one performance, transition or product beat with a composed ending.

features.title: Opening and optional end image
features.body: Guide subject identity and framing with a source image, then add an ending image when the destination composition matters. Keep camera direction compatible with both anchors.

features.title: Dedicated audio-to-video
features.body: A2V requires a private audio asset and can use an optional image. Pricing follows trusted input-audio duration, which keeps the model page, preflight and final generation on the same factual basis.

decisionCards.title: Best fit: locked production concepts
decisionCards.body: Use Pro for approved campaign beats, product sequences and character performances with clear identity, action, camera and delivery requirements.

decisionCards.title: Not ideal: broad prompt exploration
decisionCards.body: If the team is still comparing compositions or motion ideas, use Fast first and bring only the strongest controlled brief into Pro.

decisionCards.title: Protect production anchors
decisionCards.body: Name the subject traits, material behavior, screen direction and final frame that cannot drift. Remove secondary events that compete with the primary action.

referenceWorkflows.title: Text production
referenceWorkflows.body: Write a concise shot brief with one central action and an explicit landing composition.

referenceWorkflows.title: Image production
referenceWorkflows.body: Preserve the source and direct camera, timing and environmental response around it.

referenceWorkflows.title: Audio performance
referenceWorkflows.body: Map visible beats to an owned source clip and let its validated duration define the billed quantity.

referenceWorkflows.title: Production safety
referenceWorkflows.body: Verify media rights, likeness consent, anatomy, text, logos and content safety before approval.

tabs.label: Production
tabs.title: Lock the deliverable
tabs.description: State what the approved shot must communicate and preserve.
tabs.copy:
Deliverable:
[Campaign beat, product motion or character performance]

Subject anchors:
[Identity, wardrobe, shape, materials and props]

Primary action:
[One physically readable change]

Final composition:
[Framing, pose and visual priority]

tabs.label: Camera
tabs.title: Specify controlled cinematography
tabs.description: Connect camera movement, light and action into one shot.
tabs.copy:
Opening frame:
[Shot size, lens feel and light]

Camera path:
[One precise move and speed]

Physical response:
[Weight, contact, cloth, hair, reflections or particles]

Continuity:
[Screen direction and details that stay unchanged]

tabs.label: Audio
tabs.title: Map source audio to performance
tabs.description: Use visible beats that correspond to the owned clip.
tabs.copy:
Source clip:
[Owned audio asset and verified duration]

Cue map:
[Opening, accent and closing moments]

Performance:
[Gesture, expression or scene change for each cue]

Avoid:
[Extra cuts, identity drift, malformed anatomy, captions and watermarks]

tabNotes.body: A production prompt should make approval criteria visible rather than relying on broad adjectives.
One motivated camera move usually protects continuity better than several competing moves.
Source-audio duration is a trusted media fact and never a free-form client pricing field.

globalPrinciples: Remove actions that do not support the delivery goal.
Repeat only the identity and continuity anchors that must not change.
Use a clear final beat for editorial usability.
Confirm rights, consent and safety before using any source media.
engineWhy: Pro provides the current production default for the LTX family.
Dedicated text, image and audio modes keep required inputs explicit.
Bounded output choices encourage a focused shot that reviewers can evaluate consistently.

demo.title: LTX 2.5 Pro production shot
demo.prompt: A brushed-steel espresso machine stands on a dark walnut counter in a quiet café before opening. A barista locks the portafilter into place, steam briefly curls in the side light, and the camera performs a slow push toward the polished control dial. Preserve machine geometry, hand anatomy and reflected window lines. End on a stable close three-quarter composition without labels or logos.
notes: Contact and reflections create concrete fidelity checks.
The final close composition is specified for editorial usability.

proofItems.title: Production fidelity
proofItems.body: Inspect protected materials, shapes and subject identity.

proofItems.title: Physical motion
proofItems.body: Check contact, weight, timing and environmental response.

proofItems.title: Audio performance
proofItems.body: Review alignment between source cues and visible action.

proofItems.title: Stable ending
proofItems.body: Confirm the final beat is composed and useful in an edit.

proofItems.title: Approval safety
proofItems.body: Reject rights issues, unsafe imagery, accidental marks and deceptive likenesses.
